name: omni-v2
note: Omnidirectional retrain, 2026-09-19, direct train.py, 5000 iterations, with NEW payload_mass domain randomization (0-200g added at torso COM, randomized per parallel env) on top of the pre-existing foot_friction randomization -- per the user's request that a single-friction/single-payload training run was insufficient. Same pattern as before held: fell_over stayed lowest right around iteration 700 (avg 0.06 across the friction+payload-randomized episodes, error_vel_xy=0.18) and got noisier with further training, so this is again the iteration-700 checkpoint, not the run's final one. Unlike omni-v1's 0.0 fell_over, this figure is now measured across randomized payload/friction rather than one fixed condition, so it is not a regression -- it reflects the same policy quality under a harder, more realistic test. `name` kept <=16 chars for saveUploaded().

name: omni-v1
note: Omnidirectional (forward/back/left/right, not just forward+turn) retrain, 2026-09-19. walking-kxr-rl's own tools/train_all.py, KXR_OMNI_RANGE=0.3 (this robot's own measured v_max, ~0.32 m/s, so the full requested range). Deliberately the BASE checkpoint (700 iterations, no extension): three independent runs each reached Episode_Termination/fell_over=0.0 with Metrics/twist/error_vel_xy~0.18 right at 700 iterations, then destabilized (fell_over up to 0.17-0.21) every time training continued past it -- the extension chunks this robot's own training kept trying were making things worse, not better. `name` is intentionally short (this firmware's own saveUploaded() reuses it as the flash save name: letters/digits/-/_ only, <=16 chars -- see policy.h's own validSavedName() comment).
